newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil farms into Gulf of Mexico area.
newsitem.headline: Statoil farms into Gulf of Mexico area.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had acquired a 35 percent stake in the Fuji exploration area in the Gulf of Mexico, where operator Texaco Inc is planning to spud two wells this year.
The area lies in about 1,300 metres of water in the U.S. sector, around 280 kilometres southwest of New Orleans. The farm-in leaves Texaco with a 65 percent holding.
"An interesting hydrocarbon strike on Fuji block 506 in 1995 helped to reduce the risk of other relevant prospects in the area," Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said.
Texaco is due to spud one well on block 505 in February, with a second likely in the second half of the year.
Egil Endresen, head of Statoil's operations in Houston, said the area could prove to contain a few hundred million barrels of recoverable oil.
Statoil's operations in deep Mexican Gulf waters share features with deepwater exploration off Norway, Endresen said.
"If a commercial discovery is made, production could begin around 2000," the newsletter said.
